q: The randomised quicksort algorithm has expected O(n log n) comparisons. The information-theoretic argument uses the fact that the algorithm gains at least how much information per comparison?
opts: 1 bit (each comparison is a binary question)
exp: Each comparison is a binary yes/no answer, providing at most 1 bit. Since sorting requires at least log₂(n!) ≈ n log n bits total, and each comparison gives ≤ 1 bit, any comparison-based sort needs ≥ n log n comparisons. Quicksort achieves this optimum in expectation.
